newsitem.title: UK: British-Borneo gains after analysts meet.
newsitem.headline: British-Borneo gains after analysts meet.

text.p: British-Borneo Petroleum Syndicate Plc advanced 54 pence to 1,260 pence as its impressive new year rally gained extra momentum following a presentation to analysts late on Wednesday.
"They talked about the way they were building the deep water operations in the Gulf of Mexico," said an analyst who was at the meeting.
"They conveyed their excitement about the potential of that business, given their acreage and their ability to do more deals."
The presentation was organised by the London Oil Analysts Group.
British-Borneo started powering ahead on January 7 and has gained just over 58 percent since then, while the sector as a whole has moved only 8.3 percent forward.
This recent strength in British-Borneo followed news of an exploration deal with British Petroleum and reserve upgrades of the fully owned Morpeth field in the Gulf of Mexico.

Several broker buy recommendations and vague bid talk -- which has already dissipated -- gave the shares an extra lift. The rise has been viewed with wariness by several analysts and British-Borneo failed to convince all of them yesterday that the current share price was justified.
"There comes a point where you have to prove that the market optimism is well founded," said analyst Jurjen Lunshof at Credit Lyonnais Laing.
British-Borneo is an exploration company. It has not pumped up oil in commercial quantities yet.
